subject: Hosted API tier uplift + per-route rate band rework
content:
From: Jane Holloway <jane.holloway@brightlayer.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: raise hosted API commit + burst/rate limits

Hi Marcus,

We’re coming up on BrightLayer’s Q1 planning and we expect a material step-up in inference traffic for our recommendation API during the holiday load window. Current hosted plan is a 5M monthly token commit; we’d like to discuss moving to ~12M/mo and increasing per-minute rate bands (we currently hit the soft throttle around 250 requests/min on our busiest routes).

Questions:
- Can Redwood accommodate a short-term burst window of 2x baseline qps for 10 hours/day over a 6-week period?
- What would the pricing look like for a 12M committed monthly plan (12 month term) vs a 6-month term?
- Any impact on rate limits / per-route throttles or SLOs we should plan for?

Procurement wants the ball rolling by next week so we can complete the PO — looping in procurement@brightlayer.com for that thread.

Thanks,
Jane Holloway
Head of Product
BrightLayer Inc.

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jane Holloway <jane.holloway@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: raise hosted API commit + burst/rate limits

Jane — great to hear the ramp is coming. Short answer: yes, we can support the uplift and a temporary burst window, but we need to pin down a few configuration points so we scope the right commit and rate bands.

Proposed next steps (quick):
1) Option A — 12M/mo commit, 12-month term. This gives you 15% unit discount vs current hosted list and a 2x burst allowance for pre-scheduled windows (up to 12 hours/day) with a 30% overage cap at committed rates.
2) Option B — 12M/mo, 6-month term. 8% discount, burst allowed but requires two-week notice before heavy windows and overage charged at on-demand rates.
3) Short ramp pilot — we can enable a 4-week pilot at 9M/mo to validate traffic shape + per-route limits, then auto-upgrade when you confirm. No additional setup fee.

Technical caveats (Laura):
- Per-route hard throttles are currently enforced at the tenant level; we can carve out elevated per-route qps for specific endpoints if you provide the route list and expected p95 payload length.
- KV/prefix caching will help reduce token consumption on repeated prompts.

I’ve attached a draft SOW and a rate-band estimate (rateband-estimate-4392.xlsx). Karthik — I left pricing details for you to confirm fully; Neha, can you note the recommended billing cadence and credit terms for an annual vs 6-month commitment?

If that works I’ll get a DocuSign addendum together and we can target a 2026-12-01 service change date.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: raise hosted API commit + burst/rate limits

Quick technical note for the pricing/ops docs:
- Recommended model: rwd-alpha-2.7B for recommendations (best cost/latency balance). For the 2x burst profile you mentioned, we should enforce a route-level QPS cap and shard the most expensive rerank routes to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Suggest per-route elevated limit for /v1/recommend and /v1/rerank only; leave other routes at standard throttle.
- If BrightLayer uses KV caching and sets a 120s cache TTL on user-context prefixes, we estimate ~18% token savings during peak.

Happy to run a short load test against a staging key; if you agree, I’ll reserve a 4-hour slot.

- Laura
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jane Holloway <jane.holloway@brightlayer.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: raise hosted API commit + burst/rate limits

Jane — pricing detail so procurement can start the PO:
- 12M/mo, 12-month term: effective unit price $0.00065/token (15% off list), includes up to 40% sustained burst for scheduled windows; excess billed at $0.00085/token.
- 12M/mo, 6-month term: $0.00072/token (8% off list), burst allowed but with a scheduling window and overage at $0.00098/token.
- Pilot (4 weeks, 9M/mo): free trial credit up to 1M tokens; onboarding support included.

Billing/credits: For annual contracts we can offer a 30-day invoice term and 45-day credit on first invoice; 6-months requires net 30.

I’ve created a DocuSign template and put the draft SOW in the attachment (Redwood_SOW_v3.pdf). I’ll also issue a temporary staging key for the load test if you sign off.

Karthik
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

---
From: Jane Holloway <jane.holloway@brightlayer.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightlayer.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: raise hosted API commit + burst/rate limits

Thanks team — the numbers look reasonable. Two follow-ups from procurement and engineering:
1) Procurement wants an addendum that caps our liability and includes standard data retention language — they’ll send redlines.
2) Our infra lead asked whether per-route elevated throughput means a separate rate-limited token bucket per route or a tenant-level pooled bucket with route weights. Can you confirm the implementation so we model fallbacks correctly?

We’ll aim to sign the 12-month term if we can get the 30-day invoice and the 2x burst window assurances. I’m attaching our PO template for reference (procurement will send official PO after DocuSign).

Best,
Jane

Attachment: BrightLayer_PO_template.pdf (procurement will send official PO after DocuSign)

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jane Holloway <jane.holloway@brightlayer.com>, procurement@brightlayer.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: raise hosted API commit + burst/rate limits

Jane / procurement — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming what the ops team asked:
- Implementation: we use a tenant-level pooled token bucket with route-level weights; we can carve out dedicated route buckets for up to 3 routes (e.g., /v1/recommend, /v1/rerank, /v1/batch) to guarantee elevated QPS during scheduled windows. I’ve asked Laura to add the exact rate numbers once you send expected P95 payload sizes.
- Liability and retention: I’ve forwarded your note to our legal team; procurement can send redlines to procurement@redwood.com and I’ll coordinate.

Next steps:
1) Karthik will send DocuSign for the 12M/mo, 12-month addendum (30-day invoice).
2) Procurement sends the PO to finance@redwood.com once DocuSign is complete.
3) Laura will schedule a 4-hour load test slot and reserve staging keys.
4) Target service change: 2026-12-01 (we’ll do a staged cutover during off-peak hours).

Attachments: BrightLayer_PO_4392.pdf, rateband-estimate-4392.xlsx

Looking forward — we’ll get this live and monitored.

Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
